mechanism: Haemagglutinin-targeting antibodies/inhibitors (HA-stem mAbs: CR6261, MHAA4549A/gedivumab, VIS410, MEDI8852)
note: Pan-influenza A HA-stem antibodies that beat oseltamivir in mouse and ferret lethal challenge and cleared virus in healthy-volunteer challenge, then failed in hospitalized and outpatient trials.
label: Influenza (HA antibodies)

engagement.note: CR6261, the class prototype, protected mice dosed before or after lethal H1N1/H5N1 challenge; lung titre and survival are the read-outs.
engagement.short: CR6261 protects mice pre- and post-challenge
engagement.quote: The most potent antibody (CR6261) was protective in mice when given before and after lethal H5N1 or H1N1 challenge.

engagement.note: Healthy-volunteer H3N2 challenge: 3,600 mg MHAA4549A cut nasopharyngeal viral AUC 98% (qPCR) and 100% (TCID50), as mouse lung titres predicted.
engagement.quote: In conclusion, MHAA4549A was well tolerated and demonstrated statistically significant and substantial antiviral activity in an IAV challenge model.
engagement.judgement: Comparison is in healthy volunteers inoculated 24-36 h before dosing, the same design as the mouse/ferret therapeutic experiments (Nakamura 2013, doi:10.1016/j.chom.2013.06.004). McBride's abstract does not itself cite the mouse data; Gupta 2016 does.

engagement.note: Mice showed oseltamivir synergy; in hospitalized patients MHAA4549A added nothing to oseltamivir on viral load despite confirmed airway exposure.
engagement.short: No extra viral-load drop in patients
engagement.quote: MHAA4549A+OTV did not further reduce viral load versus placebo+OTV.
engagement.judgement: Called contra on CRANE rather than Han 2021 (CR6261 inert in H1N1 challenge, doi:10.1093/cid/ciaa1725, epub 2020, print 2021) because CRANE is earlier, in patients, and its discussion states the rodent comparison itself ('In vivo rodent models and the human challenge study demonstrated MHAA4549A activity, both alone and with OTV'). Han 2021 and Lim 2022 (outpatient monotherapy, doi:10.1093/ofid/ofab630, no viral-load effect) independently confirm the direction. Exposure in nasopharynx and trachea was confirmed (Deng 2020, doi:10.1002/jcph.1652), so this is a neutralisation failure, not a delivery failure. Registry results for NCT02293863 were posted 2018-06-18, two years before the paper.

dose.note: Ferret dose-ranging set 10-30 mg/kg prophylaxis and 30 mg/kg therapy for CR6261; no human comparison yet.
dose.quote: When administered therapeutically 1 day after challenge, 30 mg/kg CR6261 prevented death in all animals and blunted disease, as evidenced by decreased weight loss and temperature rise, reduced lung viral loads and shedding, and less lung damage.

dose.model: Mouse infection-model exposure scaled by cynomolgus PK
dose.note: Mouse efficacious exposure plus cynomolgus PK projected 15-45 mg/kg; the 3,600 mg (~45 mg/kg) challenge dose was the one that worked.
dose.short: Projected 15-45 mg/kg; top of range worked
dose.quote: The predicted clearance and projected efficacious doses in humans for MHAA4549A have been verified in a Phase 1 study and Phase 2a study, respectively.
dose.judgement: Abstract-level. Gupta's 'verified' rests on then-unpublished phase 2a data (later McBride 2017): 1,200 mg (~15 mg/kg) was not significant, so only the upper bound of the projection held, hence within_2x not direction_only. In CRANE, exposure was confirmed in serum, nasopharynx and trachea (Deng 2020; t1/2 17.8-19.0 d in patients vs 22.5-23.7 d in healthy adults, Lim 2016 doi:10.1128/AAC.00607-16) and the CRANE authors state lack of exposure is unlikely to account for the lack of efficacy, so the 2020 failure is scored on efficacy, not dose.

efficacy.note: Survival after lethal challenge is the pivotal read-out; ferrets (2010) and head-to-head wins over oseltamivir in mice/ferrets (2013) followed.
efficacy.quote: The most potent antibody (CR6261) was protective in mice when given before and after lethal H5N1 or H1N1 challenge.
efficacy.judgement: Strip opens with the first clinical-candidate antibody of the class. The murine prototype stem antibody C179 protected mice in the early 1990s (Okuno et al.), but it was never a drug candidate and was not verified here, so it is not used as the opener.

efficacy.note: Challenge volunteers given MHAA4549A 24-36 h post-inoculation had lower symptom scores and mucus weight, matching mouse weight-loss/survival benefit.
efficacy.quote: Peak viral load, duration of viral shedding, influenza symptom scores, mucus weight, and inflammatory biomarkers were also reduced.
efficacy.judgement: Healthy-volunteer challenge, not patients (see subjects). Hershberger 2019 (doi:10.1016/j.ebiom.2018.12.051) later extended the match to outpatients for VIS410 (FLU-PRO lower on days 3-4, p<0.023; shedding resolved 1.9 vs 3.6 d) but that was not a status change, so no 2019 entry.

efficacy.note: Mice/ferrets: beats oseltamivir and synergises with it; hospitalized patients: no benefit at 3,600 or 8,400 mg over oseltamivir, stopped for futility.
efficacy.quote: In hospitalized patients with influenza A virus infection, MHAA4549A did not improve clinical outcomes over OTV alone.
efficacy.judgement: Contra is class-wide, not gedivumab-specific: MEDI8852+oseltamivir gave no extra shedding reduction in outpatients (Ali 2018, doi:10.1128/AAC.00694-18), CR6261 was inert in H1N1 challenge (Han 2021), and MHAA4549A failed in outpatients too (Lim 2022 OFID). The source blames timing (infection-to-treatment interval controlled at 24-36 h in animals and challenge, unknown in natural infection), older comorbid hosts and lower-airway virus, i.e. the model never tested the patients the class was aimed at. The VIS410 hospitalized phase 2b (NCT03040141) has no peer-reviewed publication that I found.

safety.note: Only cynomolgus (5, 100 mg/kg) and mouse single-dose work is published; no animal-versus-patient safety comparison exists for the class.
safety.quote: Pharmacokinetics (PK) of MHAA4549A and its related antibodies were determined in DBA/2J and Balb-c mice at 5 mg/kg and in cynomolgus monkeys at 5 and 100 mg/kg as a single intravenous dose.
safety.judgement: Human safety was benign for MHAA4549A (up to 10,800 mg, Lim 2016), CR6261 (Han 2021) and MEDI8852 (Ali 2018). VIS410 produced dose-related GI events (diarrhoea in 55% at 4,000 mg vs 24% placebo, Hershberger 2019) with IL-8/TNF-alpha rises that needed diphenhydramine/ibuprofen premedication (Sloan 2020, doi:10.1016/j.antiviral.2020.104763); no published animal study predicted or addressed this, so it cannot be scored contra under rule 1. A reviewer with the IND toxicology package could re-score.
